Application Materials.content:
You will need to provide the following documentation as part of your application. This list of documents may vary slightly from course to course.
- **Academic qualifications:** Please provide a transcript for your degree study. If you have not yet completed your degree please provide a transcript of your results achieved to date. If you have completed more than one university qualification, please provide a transcript and certificate for both.
- If your degree was awarded by a UK university, please upload a transcript of your marks for each year or an electronic Higher Education Achievement Reports (HEAR).
- If your degree was awarded by an overseas institution, you should supply a transcript of your marks for each year of your studies and a copy of your degree certificate together with a certified translation if the document is not in English. International and EU applicants are also advised to include high school transcripts.
- We accept copies of physical transcripts and degree certificates as well as electronic transcripts and certificates. Please **do not** submit originals of certificates or transcripts by post.
- If you are submitting copies of physical documents, you should upload to your application clear, colour photographs or scans of your original qualification documents (not copies or certified copies). These documents must confirm that the qualification has been awarded, show the date of the award, and show the final awarded grade.
- **Referee details:** Please provide the contact details of one or two referees on your application as required. You should provide details of an academic referee if you are currently studying, or if you have graduated within the last five years. Professional references may be considered if you have graduated more than five years ago.
- Open references will normally only be accepted if they are written on headed paper, provided as a colour copy of the original, and provide the referee’s work contact details. If you have open references, please upload these at the time of application.
- If you do not have open reference, Queen Mary will contact your referee(s) via email to supply a reference, preferably electronically. References sent by email must be sent from a university or company email address; personal email addresses such as 'Yahoo' or 'Hotmail' are not acceptable.
- Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company stamp or on official institution/company letterhead, and should be provided as a scanned colour copy of the original.
- **Statement of purpose:** Your statement of purpose should explain why you want to study your chosen programme and how it will help your future career aspirations. This should typically be one side of A4 paper.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV)/Resume**
- **English language certificate (if applicable):** If English is not your first language, you should provide evidence of English language ability: IELTS, TOEFL, or other acceptable proof. Please see the [English Language Requirements](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/) section for more details.
- You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.

Application Deadlines.content:
Dates and deadlines apply to courses delivered on site at Queen Mary University of London. If no programme-specific deadline is specified, the below deadlines apply.
- **September 2026 entry:** Applications for taught postgraduate programmes open **Monday 15 September 2025**. Deadline for postgraduate Overseas applications: **Tuesday 1 September 2026**. Welcome Week begins **Monday 14 September 2026**; Teaching begins **Monday 21 September 2026**.
- **January 2027 entry:** Deadline for postgraduate Overseas applications: **Monday 14th December 2026**. Welcome week: **Monday 18th - Friday 22nd January 2027**; Teaching begins **Monday 25th January 2027**.
- **September 2027 entry:** Applications for taught postgraduate programmes open **Monday 14 September 2026**. Deadline for postgraduate Overseas applications: **Wednesday 1 September 2027**. Welcome Week begins **Monday 20 September 2027**; Teaching begins **Monday 20 September 2027**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **UK degree requirements:** A **2:1 or above at undergraduate level in any subject**, provided the degree contains good levels of study of **Mathematics and Statistics**. Subjects likely to contain sufficient quantitative elements include Mathematics, Sciences, Engineering, Computer Science, Economics and Finance. Students from less quantitatively oriented degrees, such as Accounting, Management and Politics, are welcome if they have focused on the more quantitative elements of those degrees.
- **Other routes:** Candidates that do not currently meet the set entry requirements may also have the option to study the [Graduate Diploma in Finance and Economics](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/pathway-programmes/pmp/finance-and-economics/). Meeting the required grades on completion of this programme will provide a pathway to study MSc Business Analytics.
- **China applicants:** Queen Mary normally considers **Bachelor Degree (minimum 4 years) from selected institutions** for entry to postgraduate taught programmes. For a UK **2:1 degree**, the China equivalent is **70 to 80%**. Offer conditions will vary depending on the institution you are applying from.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language requirements for entry to postgraduate taught programmes in the School of Business and Management falls within the following English band: **Band 4: IELTS (Academic) minimum score 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking**.
Queen Mary accepts a range of English tests and qualifications categorised in its English bands to demonstrate English Language proficiency. See [all accepted English tests](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/accepted-english-language-tests-and-qualifications/) deemed equivalent to these IELTS scores.

Program Overview.content:
Business Analytics MSc is part of Business and Management, AI, Computer and Data Science, and Mathematical Sciences. With the increasing use of data in business decision making, there is a need for graduates with a strong understanding of the tools and methodologies used for business analysis. Students learn to interpret data and use the results to inform business direction, build management and leadership skills, and learn to use the principal software tools for business analysis, graduating with certifications that demonstrate practical skills.
Study options include full-time study starting September 2026 or September 2027, each lasting 1 year. The location is Mile End.
The programme is jointly run by the [School of Business and Management](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/) and [School of Mathematical Sciences](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/maths/). Students develop mathematical and statistical knowledge and gain practical experience using leading software tools. The course material aims to equip students with the skills to manage IT and analytics specialists, and to understand the leadership and organisational challenges associated with the digitisation of business processes. It examines how robust findings can be obtained from analytics and applied to the direction of businesses. The programme is taught using real-world cases from different markets and countries, and draws on the experience of an advisory group of current managers from real digital businesses. Summer placement opportunities with these industry partners may be available.
Programme structure:
- Six compulsory modules.
- Three optional modules.
- Compulsory group research project.
The Group Project in Business Analytics is the capstone module for the MSc in Business Analytics. Students work in groups to analyse a problem or question using complex data from a business context, with each group assigned a Mentor to guide the analytical problem, data organisation, analysis and presentation of results. The research project uses complex data from a business context, usually supplied by a partner company.
Teaching uses an interdisciplinary approach, including lectures led by experienced academics, Queen Mary’s Virtual Learning Environment QMplus, guest speakers, hands-on experience using industry-leading software, interactive seminars, presentations and group discussions. Students are assigned an Academic Advisor for academic and pastoral support throughout the course.
Industry and facilities features include:
- Learn from industry figures through connections with Citigroup, Nomura, Morgan Stanley, IBM and HP.
- ThinkPod interactive collaboration space with presentation, recording and video conferencing facilities.
- Free subscriptions to publications such as Bloomberg and Financial Times.
- Additional self-study content through DataCamp.
- Access to a wide range of software packages, including SAS and SPSS.
- 24-hour library on campus.
Teaching is based at Queen Mary’s [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/), one of the largest self-contained residential campuses in the capital. The Graduate Centre at Mile End provides 7,700 square metres of learning and teaching space.
The School of Business and Management is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business](https://www.aacsb.edu/about-us) (AACSB). In REF 2021, among 108 UK business schools, the School ranked 22nd for overall research quality, 28th for research outputs, 12th for research impact, and 21st for research environment.
Faculty associated with the programme include:
- [Dr Guven Demirel](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/staff/academic/profiles/demirelg.html), Reader in Supply Chain Management, whose research focuses on complex systems, including the resilience of supply networks, international business networks, and ecological networks.
- Dr Evangelos Markopoulos, Teaching Fellow (Lecturer) in Operations and Project Management, who bridges industry and academia with experience in practical research and industrial projects and initiatives.
- [Dr Sebastian del Bano Rollin](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/maths/profiles/rollinsdelbano.html), Reader in Mathematics, who previously held senior positions in investment banking focused on mathematical finance and technology for trading and risk management.
- [Dr Georg von Graevenitz](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/staff/academic/profiles/vongraevenitzg.html), Reader in Quantitative Methods and Programme Director for MSc Business Analytics, who is involved in empirical research involving trade mark data and has advised competition and regulatory authorities and international organisations.
- Dr Zeynep Gürgüç, Lecturer in Digital Economy, whose research interests include experimental and behavioural economics, applied microeconomics, game theory, digital economy, innovative technologies in energy sustainability, climate change mitigation and adaptation, and blockchain-enabled market mechanisms.
Career paths: The university’s close connections with businesses in the United Kingdom and France provide opportunities to network with practitioners during guest lectures and project work done for businesses as clients. The course provides graduates with a foundation to pursue roles in data analysis and consulting across different industries. Alumni from the course are now working in roles such as Data Science Specialist, Data Analyst, Digital Strategy Analyst, Product Specialist and Senior Business Intelligence Developer.

Curriculum.content:
The MSc in Business Analytics is available as a **full-time** course. It is taught at the University of London, within the Schools of Business and Management and the School of Mathematical Sciences on the London Campus.
Offerings:
- Business Analytics-Full Time-January (SEM2): Delivery mode **On Campus**; Duration **12 Months**.
- Business Analytics-Full Time-September (SEM1): Delivery mode **On Campus**; Duration **12 Months**.
The programme consists of **180 credits in total**: five compulsory modules each of 15 credits at level 7, three elective modules each of 15 credits at level 7, a Masterclass of 30 credits, and a Group Project of 30 credits.
Compulsory/core modules:
- MTH785P Programming for Business Analytics (term 1)
- MTH781P Data Analytics (term 1)
- BUS7061P Strategic Analysis (term 1)
- BUS7057P Leadership Skills for Business Analytics (term 1)
- BUS7064P Experiments for Business Analytics (term 2)
- BUS7052P The Masterclass in Business Analytics, core module worth **30 credits** (Semesters 1 & 2)
- BUS7051P Group Project worth **30 credits** (term 3) (core)
- BUS7140P Introduction to Mathematics and Statistics for Business (term 1), **0 credits**
Level 7 structure:
| Category | Credits | Modules |
|---|---:|---|
| Core, compulsory and guided elective | 150 | |
| Compulsory | 105 | BUS7052P - Masterclass in Business Analytics; BUS7057P - Leadership Skills for Business Analytics; BUS7061P - Strategic Analysis; MTH781P - Data Analytics; MTH785P - Programming for Business Analytics; BUS7064P - Experiments for Business and Analytics; BUS7140P - Introduction to Mathematics and Statistics for Business |
| Guided elective | 45 | MTH782P - SAS for Business Intelligence; BUS7005P - Project Management; MTH783P - Time Series Analysis for Business; MTH792P - Financial Data Analytics; MTH784P - Optimisation for Business Processes; BUS7053P - Complex Networks and Innovation; BUS7093P - Entrepreneurship for Digital Technologies; BUS7088P - Digital Business, Innovation and Transparency |
| Dissertation / project | 30 | BUS7051P - Group Project in Business Analytics |
In project based course units (Masterclass and Group Project) students work together to acquire team working skills and knowledge. Work in the Masterclass and the Group Project is examined on the basis of a written report, a formal oral presentation, and a demonstration of the insights from analysis carried by the students.

Financial Aid.content:
At the School of Business and Management, Queen Mary offers a broad range of scholarships and bursaries to support outstanding students, including those advancing to postgraduate study.
- [**President's Global Scholarships**](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/presidents-global-scholarships-postgraduate-taught.html): offering **£10,000** to highly qualified postgraduate taught offer holders joining in **September 2026**. Please see the scholarship database for full eligibility.
- [**Global Excellence Scholarship**](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/global-excellence-scholarship-postgraduate-taught.html): worth **£7,000** for high achieving postgraduate taught offer holders joining in **September 2026/27**. The Scholarship is available to all eligible international students with an offer for an eligible postgraduate taught programme.
- [**Global Talent Scholarship**](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/global-talent-scholarship--postgraduate-taught-september-2026.html): this **£5,000** scholarship supports high-achieving international students enrolling on master’s programmes in **September 2025/26**. You must hold an offer before applying. Global Talent Scholarships worth **£5,000** are also available for highly qualified postgraduate taught offer holders joining in **January 2026**.
- [**Masters Scholarship**](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/masters-scholarships-1.html) (Home Students): available to Home students with an offer for an eligible postgraduate taught programme at the School of Business and Management.
- **Chevening Awards**: Queen Mary is a partner of the UK Government’s Chevening programme, offering fully funded scholarships to students from around the world. These cover tuition fees, living costs and return travel to the UK.
- **Queen Mary Alumni Loyalty Award**: Queen Mary graduates who return for a full postgraduate degree may be eligible for a **10% tuition fee discount**.
Students can use Queen Mary’s scholarships and bursaries database to explore funding options: [Search and apply](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/database/).

Multiple Applications.content: You may apply for a **maximum of two taught programmes** or **one taught and one research programme** at Queen Mary per application cycle. Please note that you can only study for one qualification at a time, so if you receive offers for both programmes you will be required to accept one and decline the other.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: The withdrawal and deferral process differs depending on your programme level and your enrolment status. However, if you were accepted through Clearing then you cannot defer and will need to decline your offer and apply via the main application cycle. Please consider the deferral deadlines which are published online for [Postgraduate Taught](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/deadlines/) programmes. You can refer to our [Enrolment FAQs](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/newstudents/faqs/enrolment/) which set out in more detail the withdrawal and deferral processes.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
This policy applies to admission to all undergraduate, postgraduate (taught and research) programmes at Queen Mary University of London where the Queen Mary central Admissions team is responsible for administration of the admissions process, except for listed Medicine and Dentistry exclusions.
- **Conditional offer** – the offer includes conditions which the applicant must achieve before their place on the programme is confirmed. Conditions may include achievement of minimum grades, academic qualifications, English language qualifications and scores, and non-academic requirements, such as confirmation of scholarship funding.
- **Alternative offer (change of course offer)** – an alternative offer may be made where the applicant is not qualified for the programme for which they applied, but a different course, which may be at a lower level (e.g. Pre-Masters, Foundation) or may have lower entry requirements, is available. This is not offered automatically in all circumstances and offered based on agreed criteria of the programme or at the discretion of the admissions office in consultation with the Director of Admissions or Academic School.
- Applicants holding conditional offers will be informed of the procedure for submitting evidence that they have met their offer conditions, in the form of qualification documents or other evidence. Queen Mary matches the qualifications and grades achieved to the conditions specified in the offer. Where all offer conditions are met, the applicant’s place is confirmed. Where the applicant has fallen short of the offer conditions, Queen Mary may exercise discretion and confirm the place in line with agreed minimum thresholds for admission, subject to the availability of places.
- Deferred entry offers for postgraduate programmes may include English language conditions.
